newsitem.title: CROATIA: U.S. troops start arriving for Bosnia pullout.
newsitem.headline: U.S. troops start arriving for Bosnia pullout.

text.p: The first 510 of the 5,000 U.S. troops assigned to cover a withdrawal of American peacekeeping forces from Bosnia arrived in neighbouring Croatia on Sunday, U.S. officers said.
Captain Steve Metz said the advance party crossed into Croatia from Hungary and was due to reach a forward staging post at Slavonski Brod on Croatia's border with Bosnia later in the day.
"They will spend the night in Brod, do maintenance work on their vehicles on Monday and cross our pontoon bridge over the Sava River from Zupanja (Croatia) to Bosnia on Tuesday," he said.
Further units of the covering force will arrive over the next six weeks, he said.

Members of a 15,000-strong U.S. armoured division stationed in northeast Bosnia as part of the NATO-led peace force (IFOR) of 53,000 troops began to leave last week for their European headquarters in Germany.

NATO's one-year peace enforcement mission expires on December 20. But alliance leaders say some kind of "follow-on" force, including U.S. troops, will be needed next year because Bosnia's peace process remains fragile.
U.S. President Bill Clinton promised the American people ahead of elections on November 5 that U.S. troops in the current mission would be withdrawn on schedule.
The start of the withdrawal had been set back by a delay in postwar municipal elections, now set for late November, which NATO troops must secure against possible nationalist violence.
The "covering force" of 5,000 U.S. troops safeguarding the pullout is due to stay in Bosnia until next March at the latest.
